idea: Build a driving scene from independent layers: moving environment, car prop/set, driver actor, passenger actor, front-of-actor occluders such as dashboard/glass, and optional weather/light/foreground motion.

composition.notes: Road/city/landscape moves behind the scene. Prefer a loopable or long plate.
Car or car-interior set is independent from the bears and can bob/scale/shift as a whole.
Select one pose from the driver's four-pose sheet and place it into the car.
Select one pose independently from the passenger's four-pose sheet.
Steering wheel, dashboard, windshield frame or glass can sit in front of actors for believable depth.
Blurred poles, guardrails, rain, branches or light streaks sell speed.
Headlights, neon, moonlight or street lamps affect the scene without fusing asset roles.

reuse: Use the character-free car-front-seat scene template plus two independent typed four-pose actor sheets. Match poses mechanically to driver/passenger slots before rendering.
avoid: fusing bears into the car asset
using a whole-scene still when independent actor pose changes are needed
regenerating the whole scene for every shot
